sources.entry: Fossil - Distributed version control system featuring wiki and bug tracker. BSD-2-Clause-FreeBSD C

summary.name: Fossil
summary.one_liner: Fossil is a self-contained distributed version control system that also bundles bug tracking, a wiki, forum, chat, and a built-in web interface in a single executable.
use_cases: self-hosting a software project with code, wiki and bug tracker
running a project website from a repository
version control over unreliable or restricted networks
lightweight hosting on a small VPS or Raspberry Pi
summary.what_it_does: Fossil provides distributed version control similar to Git and Mercurial, along with bug tracking, a wiki, forum, email alerts, chat, and technotes. It includes a built-in, themeable web interface that serves the project's website, and the repository itself contains the wiki and documentation. Storage uses an SQLite database so transactions are atomic, and automatic self-checks run before each commit. Network communication uses HTTPS or SSH, and an autosync mode is offered to reduce needless forking and merging.
notable: All-in-one: one self-contained executable with bug tracker, wiki, forum and web UI built in
Stores repositories in SQLite with atomic transactions and pre-commit consistency checks
Network protocol is bandwidth-efficient and works over HTTPS or SSH behind firewalls
Can set up an automatic GitHub mirror
caveats: Page does not list features beyond the summarized set; no hosted service pricing is given
